title: Safely Wrapping C Strings
goal: Convert a raw C string pointer into a safe Rust string slice with minimal unsafe surface.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: FFI and C Strings

hints: Only operations that dereference raw pointers require an `unsafe` block.
Always check if a raw pointer is null before passing it to `CStr::from_ptr`.
explanation: Only `CStr::from_ptr` requires an `unsafe` block because it dereferences a raw pointer. Calling `CStr::from_ptr` without `unsafe` causes a compilation error `E0133`. Failing to check `p.is_null()` causes undefined behavior when passed a null pointer. The `c.to_str()` method is safe because it validates UTF-8.
